greek: καὶ εἶπεν κύριος πρὸς Μωυσῆν Ἤδη ὄψει ἃ ποιήσω τῷ Φαραω· ἐν γὰρ χειρὶ κραταιᾷ ἐξαποστελεῖ αὐτοὺς καὶ ἐν βραχίονι ὑψηλῷ ἐκβαλεῖ αὐτοὺς ἐκ τῆς γῆς αὐτοῦ.
hint: The lord tells Moses he will now see what is done to Pharaoh, who will be made to send the people out of his land.

notes.text: With a high arm: the Hebrew has bĕyād ḥăzāqâ, with a strong hand, at both clauses; the Greek has the strong hand at the first only.
The future of ὁράω, you will see, not the dative of ὄψις.
βραχίων, the arm: Middle Liddell's one translation, plain text, ἐν taking a unit of its own.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[lord|lord / master, the head, master, the Lord, Jehovah|κύριος]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Μωυσῆν]] [[by this time|by this time, before this, already, now and presently and forthwith, directly|ἤδη]] [[you will see|you will see, you will perceive, you will behold, you will look at|ὁράω]] which [[I will make|I will make, I will do, I will produce, I will create|ποιέω]] to the [[name:Φαραω]]; [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]], [[in hand|within, inside of, and by means of hand, hand and arm, arm|ἐν; χείρ]] [[to strong|to strong and mighty and resistless|κραταιός]] [[will send quite away|will send quite away, will dispatch|ἐξαποστέλλω]] them and [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to arm [[to high|to high and lofty and high-raised, to highland, to stately|ὑψηλός]] [[will throw|will throw, will cast out of, will throw out, will cast out and banish, will depose, will throw away and reject|ἐκβάλλω]] them [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of the earth|of the earth, of the land, of the ground|γῆ]] of him.

names.gloss: (Μωυσῆς, from Hebrew Mōšeh, which the Hebrew of 2:10 hears in māšâ, "to draw out")
(Φαραω, from Hebrew Parʿōh, from the Egyptian for "great house")

greek: Ἐλάλησεν δὲ ὁ θεὸς πρὸς Μωυσῆν καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν Ἐγὼ κύριος·
hint: God speaks to Moses and names himself: the lord.

notes.text: I, lord, without a verb: the Hebrew ʾănî YHWH, the name given as κύριος.

reading: [[talked|talked, chatted, prattled, babbled, said, talked of, spoke, chattered, chirped|λαλέω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Μωυσῆν]] and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] him I [[lord|lord / master, the head, master, the Lord, Jehovah|κύριος]];

greek: καὶ ὤφθην πρὸς Αβρααμ καὶ Ισαακ καὶ Ιακωβ, θεὸς ὢν αὐτῶν, καὶ τὸ ὄνομά μου κύριος οὐκ ἐδήλωσα αὐτοῖς·
hint: God says he appeared to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob as their God, but did not make his name 'lord' known to them.

notes.text: Being their God: the Hebrew has bĕʾēl šaddāy, as El Shaddai.
I did not make known, active: the Hebrew has lōʾ nôdaʿtî, I was not known.
The aorist passive with πρός and the accusative: I was seen toward them.

reading: and [[I was seen|I was seen, I was looked at, I was beheld and perceived and observed, I was looked out for|ὁράω]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] and [[name:Ισαακ]] and [[name:Ιακωβ]], [[God|everything that God is by nature, deity in full and undiminished kind|θεός]] being of them, and [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of me [[lord|lord / master, the head, master, the Lord, Jehovah|κύριος]] not [[I made visible|I made visible and manifest and showed and exhibited, I made known and disclosed and revealed, I proved, I declared and explained and set forth and indicated and signified, I was clear and plain|δηλόω]] to them;

names.gloss: (Αβρααμ, from Hebrew ʾAbrāhām, which the Hebrew of Genesis 17:5 hears in ʾab hămôn gôyim, "father of a multitude of nations")
(Ισαακ, from Hebrew Yiṣḥāq, "he laughs")
(Ιακωβ, from Hebrew Yaʿăqōb, which the Hebrew of Genesis 25:26 hears in ʿāqēb, "heel")

greek: καὶ ἔστησα τὴν διαθήκην μου πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὥστε δοῦναι αὐτοῖς τὴν γῆν τῶν Χαναναίων, τὴν γῆν, ἣν παρῳκήκασιν, ἐν ᾗ καὶ παρῴκησαν ἐπʼ αὐτῆς.
hint: God recalls the covenant he set with the patriarchs to give them Canaan, where they had lived as sojourners.

notes.text: The land of the Canaanites: the Hebrew has ʾereṣ kĕnāʿan, the land of Canaan.
The relative and then the pronoun again, after the Hebrew ʾăšer … bāh.
καί as the adverb, also.

reading: and [[I made to stand|I made to stand, I set, I stopped and stayed and checked, I set up and raised, I established and instituted, I appointed, I weighed|ἵστημι]] [[the disposition|the disposition of property by will, the will and testament, the arrangement between two parties, the covenant|διαθήκη]] of me [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] them [[so as to|so as to, as to, on the condition that, and so and therefore and consequently, as and as being, since it was|ὥστε]] [[to give|to give, to grant, to provide, to give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] to them [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]] of the [[name:Χαναναίων]], [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]], which [[have dwelt beside|have dwelt beside and it stands so, have dwelt along the coast of and it stands so, have lived near and it stands so, have dwelt among and it stands so, have lain near and it stands so, have lived in and sojourned and it stands so|παροικέω]], [[in which|within, inside of, and by means of which|ἐν; ὅς]] [[also|also and even, but, nay, and yet, as, likewise|καί]] [[dwelt beside|dwelt beside, dwelt along the coast of, lived near, dwelt among, lay near, lived in and sojourned|παροικέω]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] of her.

names.gloss: (Χαναναῖος, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿănî, "of Canaan")

greek: καὶ ἐγὼ εἰσήκουσα τὸν στεναγμὸν τῶν υἱῶν Ισραηλ, ὃν οἱ Αἰγύπτιοι καταδουλοῦνται αὐτούς, καὶ ἐμνήσθην τῆς διαθήκης ὑμῶν.
hint: God has heard Israel groaning under Egyptian slavery and has remembered the covenant.

notes.text: Your covenant: the Hebrew has bĕrîtî, my covenant.
ὅν agrees with στεναγμόν; αὐτούς, the sons, is the object: the groaning with which the Egyptians enslave them.

reading: and I [[I hearkened|I hearkened and gave ear to, I heard, I hearkened to and gave heed to|εἰσακούω]] [[the sighing|the sighing and groaning and moaning|στεναγμός]] of the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]], which the [[name:Αἰγύπτιοι]] [[are being reduced to slavery|are being reduced to slavery and enslaved, are making slaves to themselves and enslaving, are enslaving in mind|καταδουλόω]] them, and [[I reminded myself of|I reminded myself of, I called to mind, I remembered, I bethought myself of, I was minded, I bore in mind and did not forget, I mentioned and made mention of|μιμνήσκομαι]] [[of the disposition|of the disposition of property by will, of the will and testament, of the arrangement between two parties, of the covenant|διαθήκη]] of you.

names.gloss: (Ισραηλ, from Hebrew Yiśrāʾēl, which the Hebrew of Genesis 32:29 hears in śārâ ʿim ʾĕlōhîm, "he strove with God")
(Αἰγύπτιος, the man of Αἴγυπτος, Egypt)

greek: βάδιζε εἰπὸν τοῖς υἱοῖς Ισραηλ λέγων Ἐγὼ κύριος καὶ ἐξάξω ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τῆς δυναστείας τῶν Αἰγυπτίων καὶ ῥύσομαι ὑμᾶς ἐκ τῆς δουλείας καὶ λυτρώσομαι ὑμᾶς ἐν βραχίονι ὑψηλῷ καὶ κρίσει μεγάλῃ
hint: Moses is to tell Israel that the lord will bring them out of Egypt's power and ransom them with a high arm.

notes.text: Go: the Hebrew has lākēn, therefore.
From the lordship of the Egyptians: the Hebrew has mittaḥat siblōt miṣrayim, from under the burdens of Egypt.

notes.lemma: ἐν βραχίονι ὑψηλῷ καὶ κρίσει μεγάλῃ
notes.text: With a high arm and great judgment: the Hebrew has bizrôaʿ nĕṭûyâ ûbišpāṭîm gĕdōlîm, with an outstretched arm and great judgments.
λυτρόω, to release on receipt of ransom: Middle Liddell gives the active and the passive; this is the future middle.

reading: [[go slowly|go slowly and walk, go and march, go by land, enter, proceed|βαδίζω]] [[say|say, speak, declare, call by name, tell|λέγω]] to the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling|λέγω]] I [[lord|lord / master, the head, master, the Lord, Jehovah|κύριος]] and [[I will lead out|I will lead out, I will lead and carry out from, I will bring forth into the world, I will march out, I will eject, I will carry out and export, I will draw off, I will call forth and excite, I will lead on and tempt|ἐξάγω]] you [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of the power|of the power and lordship and sovereignty, of the oligarchy|δυναστεία]] of the [[name:Αἰγυπτίων]] and [[I will draw to myself|I will draw to myself, I will draw out of danger and rescue and save and deliver, I will save, I will save from an illness and cure, I will set free and redeem, I will shield and guard and protect, I will deliver, I will remove, I will draw back and hold back and check, I will keep off|ῥύομαι]] you [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of the servitude|of the servitude and slavery and bondage, of the slaves and the slave-class|δουλεία]] and [[I will release on receipt of ransom|I will release on receipt of ransom and hold to ransom|λυτρόω]] you [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to arm [[to high|to high and lofty and high-raised, to highland, to stately|ὑψηλός]] and [[to a separating|to a separating and power of distinguishing, to choice and selection, to a decision and judgment, to means of judging, to a trial, to the result of a trial and condemnation, to a dispute, to the event and issue|κρίσις]] [[to big|to big, to great, to tall, to full-grown, to vast and high, to spacious and wide, to strong and mighty, to violent, to loud, to prevailing, to weighty and important|μέγας]]

greek: καὶ λήμψομαι ἐμαυτῷ ὑμᾶς λαὸν ἐμοὶ καὶ ἔσομαι ὑμῶν θεός, καὶ γνώσεσθε ὅτι ἐγὼ κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὑμῶν ὁ ἐξαγαγὼν ὑμᾶς ἐκ τῆς καταδυναστείας τῶν Αἰγυπτίων,
hint: God will take Israel as his people and be their God, and they will know who led them out from oppression.

notes.text: From the oppression of the Egyptians: the Hebrew has mittaḥat siblōt miṣrayim, from under the burdens of Egypt. καταδυναστεία, not in Middle Liddell, is LSJ's oppression, one translation, plain text.
I will be your God: θεός without the article, the predicate.

reading: and [[I will take|I will take, I will receive, I will take hold of and grasp and seize|λαμβάνω]] to myself you [[a people|a people, men, soldiers, a land-army, the common men, folk, Jews, Christians|λαός]] to me and I will be of you [[God|everything that God is by nature, deity in full and undiminished kind|θεός]], and [[you will learn to know|you will learn to know, you will perceive, you will mark, you will learn, you will discern and distinguish|γινώσκω]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] I [[lord|lord / master, the head, master, the Lord, Jehovah|κύριος]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] of you [[the one having led out|the one having led out, having led and carried out from, having brought forth into the world, having marched out, having ejected, having carried out and exported, having drawn off, having called forth and excited, having led on and tempted|ἐξάγω]] you [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] of the oppression of the [[name:Αἰγυπτίων]],

greek: καὶ εἰσάξω ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν γῆν, εἰς ἣν ἐξέτεινα τὴν χεῖρά μου δοῦναι αὐτὴν τῷ Αβρααμ καὶ Ισαακ καὶ Ιακωβ, καὶ δώσω ὑμῖν αὐτὴν ἐν κλήρῳ· ἐγὼ κύριος.
hint: God promises to bring them into the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and give it to them by lot.

notes.text: I stretched out my hand: the Hebrew has nāśāʾtî ʾet-yādî, I lifted my hand, the gesture of an oath.
In a lot, an allotment: the Hebrew has môrāšâ, a possession.

reading: and [[I will lead in|I will lead in, I will lead into and introduce, I will admit, I will import, I will call in, I will bring in and bring forward|εἰσάγω]] you [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]], [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] which [[I stretched out|I stretched out, I spread out, I put forth|ἐκτείνω]] [[the hand|the hand, the hand and arm, the arm|χείρ]] of me [[to give|to give, to grant, to provide, to give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] her to the [[name:Αβρααμ]] and to [[name:Ισαακ]] and to [[name:Ιακωβ]], and [[I will give|I will give, I will grant, I will provide, I will give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] to you her [[in a lot|within, inside of, and by means of a lot, a casting lots and drawing lots, an allotment, any piece of land and a portion and farm, the clergy|ἐν; κλῆρος]]; I [[lord|lord / master, the head, master, the Lord, Jehovah|κύριος]].

greek: ἐλάλησεν δὲ Μωυσῆς οὕτως τοῖς υἱοῖς Ισραηλ, καὶ οὐκ εἰσήκουσαν Μωυσῇ ἀπὸ τῆς ὀλιγοψυχίας καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων τῶν σκληρῶν.
hint: Moses tells the Israelites, but worn out in spirit and by hard labour they do not listen to him.

notes.text: ὀλιγοψυχία, not in Middle Liddell: LSJ points to λιποψυχία, swooning, and gives faint-heartedness, citing this verse; for the Hebrew qōṣer rûaḥ, shortness of spirit, little-souledness in the Greek's own compound.
The hard works, plural: the Hebrew ʿăbōdâ qāšâ, hard service, singular.

reading: [[talked|talked, chatted, prattled, babbled, said, talked of, spoke, chattered, chirped|λαλέω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Μωυσῆς]] [[in this way|in this way, in this manner, so, thus, even so, so much|οὕτως]] to the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]], and not [[hearkened|hearkened and gave ear to, heard, hearkened to and gave heed to|εἰσακούω]] to [[name:Μωυσῇ]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of the swooning|of the swooning, of the faint-heartedness|ὀλιγοψυχία]] and [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] [[of the works|of the works, of the business, of the deeds|ἔργον]] [[of the hard|of the hard, of the harsh and crashing, of the stiff and unyielding, of the stiff and sturdy, of the austere and severe|σκληρός]].

greek: Εἶπεν δὲ κύριος πρὸς Μωυσῆν λέγων
hint: The lord speaks to Moses.

notes.text: Saying, opening the speech of the next verse.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[lord|lord / master, the head, master, the Lord, Jehovah|κύριος]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Μωυσῆν]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling|λέγω]]

greek: Εἴσελθε λάλησον Φαραω βασιλεῖ Αἰγύπτου, ἵνα ἐξαποστείλῃ τοὺς υἱοὺς Ισραηλ ἐκ τῆς γῆς αὐτοῦ.
hint: Moses is to go in and tell Pharaoh to send the sons of Israel out of his land.

notes.text: Two imperatives without a conjunction, as the Hebrew bōʾ dabbēr.

reading: [[go in|go in, go into and enter, come into, come in, come upon|εἰσέρχομαι]] [[talk|talk, chat, prattle, babble, say, talk of, speak, chatter, chirp|λαλέω]] to [[name:Φαραω]] [[to a king|to a king and chief, to an hereditary king, to a lord and master and householder, to the second of the nine archons, to the king of Persia|βασιλεύς]] of [[name:Αἰγύπτου]], [[that|that, in order that|ἵνα]] [[may send quite away|may send quite away, may dispatch|ἐξαποστέλλω]] the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of the earth|of the earth, of the land, of the ground|γῆ]] of him.

names.gloss: (Αἴγυπτος, the Greek name of the land; Hebrew Miṣrayim)

greek: ἐλάλησεν δὲ Μωυσῆς ἔναντι κυρίου λέγων Ἰδοὺ οἱ υἱοὶ Ισραηλ οὐκ εἰσήκουσάν μου, καὶ πῶς εἰσακούσεταί μου Φαραω; ἐγὼ δὲ ἄλογός εἰμι.
hint: Moses objects that if Israel has not listened, Pharaoh will not either, since he has no gift of speech.

notes.text: I am without speech: the Hebrew has ʿăral śĕpātāyim, uncircumcised of lips.
Middle Liddell's first translation is 'without' and then the Greek λόγος: GREEK_LOST gives it whole.
ἔναντι, in the presence of: Middle Liddell's one translation, plain text.

reading: [[talked|talked, chatted, prattled, babbled, said, talked of, spoke, chattered, chirped|λαλέω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Μωυσῆς]] in the presence of [[of lord|of lord / master, of the head, of master, of the Lord, of Jehovah|κύριος]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling|λέγω]] [[lo|lo, behold, see there|ἰδού]] the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]] not [[hearkened|hearkened and gave ear to, heard, hearkened to and gave heed to|εἰσακούω]] of me, and [[how|how, in what way, in what manner|πῶς]] [[will hearken|will hearken and give ear to, will hear, will hearken to and give heed to|εἰσακούω]] of me [[name:Φαραω]]? I [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[without logos (λόγος)|without logos (λόγος), unutterable, without reason and irrational, not reckoned upon and unexpected|ἄλογος]] am.

greek: εἶπεν δὲ κύριος πρὸς Μωυσῆν καὶ Ααρων καὶ συνέταξεν αὐτοῖς πρὸς Φαραω βασιλέα Αἰγύπτου ὥστε ἐξαποστεῖλαι τοὺς υἱοὺς Ισραηλ ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου.
hint: The lord gives Moses and Aaron their charge to Pharaoh, to send Israel out of Egypt.

notes.text: He charged them toward Pharaoh: the Hebrew has wayĕṣawwēm ʾel-bĕnê yiśrāʾēl wĕʾel-parʿōh, to the sons of Israel and to Pharaoh.
So as to send away: the Hebrew has lĕhôṣîʾ, to bring out.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[lord|lord / master, the head, master, the Lord, Jehovah|κύριος]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Μωυσῆν]] and [[name:Ααρων]] and [[put in order together|put in order together, drew up and put in array, arranged and organised, concocted, fixed and assessed, ordained and prescribed|συντάσσω]] to them [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Φαραω]] [[a king|a king and chief, an hereditary king, a lord and master and householder, the second of the nine archons, the king of Persia|βασιλεύς]] of [[name:Αἰγύπτου]] [[so as to|so as to, as to, on the condition that, and so and therefore and consequently, as and as being, since it was|ὥστε]] [[to send quite away|to send quite away, to dispatch|ἐξαποστέλλω]] the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of earth|of earth, of land, of ground|γῆ]] of [[name:Αἰγύπτου]].

names.gloss: (Ααρων, from Hebrew ʾAhărōn, of uncertain meaning)

greek: Καὶ οὗτοι ἀρχηγοὶ οἴκων πατριῶν αὐτῶν. υἱοὶ Ρουβην πρωτοτόκου Ισραηλ· Ενωχ καὶ Φαλλους, Ασρων καὶ Χαρμι· αὕτη ἡ συγγένεια Ρουβην.
hint: The family heads begin with Reuben's four sons.

notes.text: Heads of the houses of their lineages, for the Hebrew rāʾšê bêt-ʾăbōtām, heads of their fathers' house. ἀρχηγός, as a noun, opens with founder.
συγγένεια, kin, singular, for the Hebrew mišpĕḥōt, families.

reading: and [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[founders|founders, princes and chiefs, first causes and originators, beginning and originating|ἀρχηγός]] [[of houses|of houses and abodes and dwellings, of rooms and chambers, of houses of a god and temples, of household goods and substances, of households and families|οἶκος]] [[of lineages|of lineages and pedigrees and by the father's side, of clans and houses and families|πατριά]] of them. sons of [[name:Ρουβην]] of first-born of [[name:Ισραηλ]]; [[name:Ενωχ]] and [[name:Φαλλους]], [[name:Ασρων]] and [[name:Χαρμι]]; [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[the sameness of descent|the sameness of descent, the family and relationship and kin, the ties of kindred and family connexion and influence, the kinsfolk and kinsmen, the families|συγγένεια]] of [[name:Ρουβην]].

names.gloss: (Ρουβην, from Hebrew Rĕʾûbēn, which the Hebrew of Genesis 29:32 hears in rāʾâ bĕʿonyî, "he has seen my affliction")
(Ενωχ, from Hebrew Ḥănôk, usually connected with ḥānak, "to dedicate")
(Φαλλους, from Hebrew Pallûʾ, of uncertain meaning)
(Ασρων, from Hebrew Ḥeṣrôn, usually connected with ḥāṣēr, "enclosure")
(Χαρμι, from Hebrew Karmî, usually connected with kerem, "vineyard")

greek: καὶ υἱοὶ Συμεων· Ιεμουηλ καὶ Ιαμιν καὶ Αωδ καὶ Ιαχιν καὶ Σααρ καὶ Σαουλ ὁ ἐκ τῆς Φοινίσσης· αὗται αἱ πατριαὶ τῶν υἱῶν Συμεων.
hint: Simeon's six sons, the last the son of a Phoenician woman.

notes.text: The one of the Phoenician woman: the Hebrew has ben-hakkĕnaʿănît, son of the Canaanite woman, and Genesis 46:10 has τῆς Χανανίτιδος.
The article over a phrase: the one from.

reading: and sons of [[name:Συμεων]]; [[name:Ιεμουηλ]] and [[name:Ιαμιν]] and [[name:Αωδ]] and [[name:Ιαχιν]] and [[name:Σααρ]] and [[name:Σαουλ]] the one [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] of the [[name:Φοινίσσης]]; [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[the lineages|the lineages and pedigrees and by the father's side, the clans and houses and families|πατριά]] of the sons of [[name:Συμεων]].

names.gloss: (Συμεων, from Hebrew Šimʿôn, which the Hebrew of Genesis 29:33 hears in šāmaʿ, "he heard")
(Ιεμουηλ, from Hebrew Yĕmûʾēl, of uncertain meaning)
(Ιαμιν, from Hebrew Yāmîn, "right hand")
(Αωδ, from Hebrew ʾŌhad, of uncertain meaning)
(Ιαχιν, from Hebrew Yākîn, "he establishes")

greek: καὶ ταῦτα τὰ ὀνόματα τῶν υἱῶν Λευι κατὰ συγγενείας αὐτῶν· Γεδσων, Κααθ καὶ Μεραρι· καὶ τὰ ἔτη τῆς ζωῆς Λευι ἑκατὸν τριάκοντα ἑπτά.
hint: Levi's three sons, and Levi's lifespan: a hundred and thirty-seven years.

notes.text: By their kindreds, for the Hebrew lĕtōlĕdōtām, by their generations.
Genesis 46:11 spells the name Γηρσων; the Hebrew is Gēršôn.

reading: and [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[the names|the names, the fames, the mere names, the phrases and expressions|ὄνομα]] of the sons of [[name:Λευι]] [[down|down, downwards, down from, down upon, over, upon|κατά + accusative]] [[samenesses of descent|samenesses of descent, families and relationships and kins, ties of kindred and family connexions and influences, kinsfolk and kinsmen, families|συγγένεια]] of them; [[name:Γεδσων]], [[name:Κααθ]] and [[name:Μεραρι]]; and the years [[of the life|of the life, of the means of life and substance, of existence, of a way of life|ζωή]] of [[name:Λευι]] hundred thirty seven.

greek: καὶ οὗτοι υἱοὶ Γεδσων· Λοβενι καὶ Σεμεϊ, οἶκοι πατριᾶς αὐτῶν.
hint: Gershon's two sons.

notes.text: Houses of their lineage, for the Hebrew lĕmišpĕḥōtām, by their families.

reading: and [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] sons of [[name:Γεδσων]]; [[name:Λοβενι]] and [[name:Σεμεϊ]], [[houses|houses and abodes and dwellings, rooms and chambers, houses of a god and temples, household goods and substances, households and families|οἶκος]] [[of lineage|of lineage and pedigree and by the father's side, of a clan and house and family|πατριά]] of them.

(Σεμεϊ, from Hebrew Šimʿî, usually connected with šāmaʿ, "to hear")

greek: καὶ υἱοὶ Κααθ· Αμβραμ καὶ Ισσααρ, Χεβρων καὶ Οζιηλ· καὶ τὰ ἔτη τῆς ζωῆς Κααθ ἑκατὸν τριάκοντα ἔτη.
hint: Kohath's four sons, and Kohath's lifespan: a hundred and thirty years.

notes.text: A hundred and thirty years: the Hebrew has a hundred and thirty-three.
For the Hebrew Yiṣhār, Izhar; Genesis 46:24 uses the same Greek spelling for a son of Naphtali, Yēṣer.

reading: and sons of [[name:Κααθ]]; [[name:Αμβραμ]] and [[name:Ισσααρ]], [[name:Χεβρων]] and [[name:Οζιηλ]]; and the years [[of the life|of the life, of the means of life and substance, of existence, of a way of life|ζωή]] of [[name:Κααθ]] hundred thirty years.

names.gloss: (Αμβραμ, from Hebrew ʿAmrām, usually explained as ʿam rām, "the kinsman is exalted")
(Ισσααρ, for Hebrew Yiṣhār, usually connected with yiṣhār, "fresh oil")
(Χεβρων, from Hebrew Ḥebrôn, usually connected with ḥeber, "association")
(Οζιηλ, from Hebrew ʿUzzîʾēl, "my strength is God")

greek: καὶ υἱοὶ Μεραρι· Μοολι καὶ Ομουσι. οὗτοι οἶκοι πατριῶν Λευι κατὰ συγγενείας αὐτῶν.
hint: Merari's two sons, closing the houses of Levi.

notes.text: Houses of the lineages of Levi, for the Hebrew mišpĕḥōt hallēwî, the families of the Levite.

reading: and sons of [[name:Μεραρι]]; [[name:Μοολι]] and [[name:Ομουσι]]. hint: Amram marries Jochebed; their children are Aaron, Moses and Miriam. Amram lives a hundred and thirty-two years.

notes.text: The daughter of his father's brother: the Hebrew has dōdātô, his father's sister.

(Μαριαμ, from Hebrew Miryām, of uncertain meaning)

notes.text: The Hebrew has Qōraḥ, Nepeg and Zikrî.

reading: and sons of [[name:Ισσααρ]]; [[name:Κορε]] and [[name:Ναφεκ]] and [[name:Ζεχρι]].

(Ναφεκ, from Hebrew Nepeg, of uncertain meaning)
(Ζεχρι, from Hebrew Zikrî, usually connected with zākar, "to remember")

notes.text: Two sons: the Hebrew has three, Mîšāʾēl first, then ʾElṣāpān and Sitrî.

reading: and sons of [[name:Οζιηλ]]; [[name:Ελισαφαν]] and [[name:Σετρι]].
